ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Luxembourg: (i) Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (SARL framework); (ii) Law of 12 November 2004 on the Fight against Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, as amended by the laws of 2015, 2019 and 2020 (implementation of EU Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843); (iii) Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Effective Beneficial Owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs – RBE); (iv) CSSF Regulation No. 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on AML/CFT; (v) Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2019 on the RBE; (vi) Law of 31 May 1999 on the domiciliation of commercial companies; (vii) applicable EU Freezing and Sanctions Regulations.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (restricted access: the RBE is accessible only to competent authorities, AML obliged entities, and persons demonstrating a legitimate interest; public access is restricted following CJEU Joined Cases C-37/20 and C-601/20 of 22 November 2022, subject to proportionality and national-security screening)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Authentic certified copy of each UBO's valid international passport or national identity card
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport/ID issuing authority of the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (where the issuing state is a 1961 Hague Convention contracting state) or consular legalization at the Luxembourg Embassy/Consulate for non-Convention states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incumbency or recent extract from the foreign business register of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial registry or Chamber of Commerce of the corporate shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, plus sworn translation into French, German, or Luxembourgish where required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Extract of criminal record (certificate of non-conviction) for each proposed statutory manager (gérant), director, and legal signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent judicial records authority (casier judiciaire) of the country of residence or nationality

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Recent proof of residential address (utility bill or municipal certificate) for each UBO and statutory officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or municipal registry office of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy, or Hague Apostille for documents originating outside the EU

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Tax residence certificate for each individual or corporate UBO where relevant to Luxembourg commercial substance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Tax administration of the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille or consular legalization where required, with sworn translation if in a non-official Luxembourg language

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory, documented screening of each UBO, statutory manager (gérant), signatory, and counterparty against: (a) EU Council consolidated financial sanctions list; (b) UN Security Council consolidated list; (c) Luxembourg national asset-freeze lists issued under the AML Law of 12 November 2004; (d) OFAC SDN list insofar as USD payment rails (Wise B2B, TikTok Creator Payout) create a US nexus; (e) UK OFSI list on a best-effort basis. PEP determination follows FATF and Directive (EU) 2015/849 categories (heads of state, senior government officials, high-ranking judicial and military officers, senior SOE executives, political-party leaders), triggering enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Screening occurs pre-incorporation and is refreshed every 12 months or upon trigger events such as new shareholders, new managers, or sanctions-list updates.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – electronic platform www.lbr.lu (maintained for the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés – RCS of the District Court of Luxembourg)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be expressed in Latin/Roman script; non-Roman scripts are not recordable and must be transliterated. Official languages are Luxembourgish, French, and German; names in French, German, Luxembourgish, or an internationally accepted language such as English are admissible if not misleading. The name must be distinctive and not identical or confusingly similar (phonetically or visually) to an existing RCS entry, and must not contravene public order or bonos mores. A SARL must state its legal form as 'Société à responsabilité limitée' or 'SARL' in all correspondence and in the RCS registration, with the legal-form token placed before or after the distinctive name element.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank – requires prior CSSF authorization under the Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector
Assurance / Insurance – requires prior authorization of the Commissariat aux Assurances
SICAV / SICAF / Fonds / FCP – reserved for regulated investment vehicles under the Law of 17 December 2010
Audit / Réviseur d'entreprises – reserved to CSSF-approved statutory auditors
Avocat / Lawyer / Notaire / Notary – reserved to members of the Luxembourg Bar and Chamber of Notaries
État / Luxembourg as a State designator / Commune / Ministère – creates a false connection with the State; requires ministerial authorization or is prohibited
Fiduciaire / Trust – implies licensed fiduciary or trust activity and triggers prior regulatory assessment
Université / École / Croix-Rouge and other public-institution names – requires institutional consent
Global / World / TikTok / MCN – generally permissible at registry level, but prior trademark clearance and social-media platform consent must be obtained separately
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection by the RCS registrar (conservateur), the applicant must within 15 days: (i) instruct the acting notary to file three alternative names through the LBR portal for a renewed distinctiveness search; (ii) if the conflict persists, submit a written reconsideration request with a memorandum of distinctiveness to the RCS service of the District Court of Luxembourg; (iii) in final instance, appeal the registrar's decision before the Commercial Chamber of the District Court of Luxembourg (Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg) within one month of notification, following the ordinary procedure for RCS decisions; (iv) where the rejection concerns a sensitive token, apply through the notary to the Minister of Justice for a derogation before filing the appeal. A reserved but unused name may be renewed once for an additional 30 days by filing a renewal request at LBR before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are permissible only where implemented as a regulated domiciliation: the SARL must maintain a real siège social in Luxembourg provided under the Law of 31 May 1999 by a Ministry of Justice-approved domiciliation agent. A pure letter-box office without a dedicated communication line, a Luxembourg bank account or Wise B2B account, local management, and annual accounting substance creates tax-residence, RBE-compliance, and reputational risk. For a TikTok MCN agency operating with remote creators, standard and acceptable substance includes a local gérant, a Luxembourg bank or payment-account connection, a proper accounting file, and annual accounts filed with the RCS; artificial diversion of Luxembourg VAT or CIT substance is not acceptable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low quantified risk of 3–5% for the first 24 months for a low-risk, non-licensed ISIC 7310 activity; probability rises materially (toward 20–35% inside a tax audit) if the income-to-substance ratio triggers a Luxembourg corporate tax, VAT, or CCSS (social security) inspection, or if the domiciliation agent itself becomes subject to supervision.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, particularly Articles 1, 9, 100-1 to 100-25, and 710-1 to 710-24 concerning the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés – RCS), operated through the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) electronic filing platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) together with the single incorporation dossier (dossier unique) filed electronically via the LBR/RCS e-filing portal and published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum issued and fully paid-up share capital of EUR 12,000 for a SARL; cash contributions must be deposited into a Luxembourg bank blocked account and certified by a certificate of deposit or blocked-funds attestation before registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers hereby form a private limited liability company (SARL) under the laws of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; that each named subscriber’s subscription and contribution to the initial share capital, as set forth in the articles of incorporation, be and is hereby approved and ratified; that the registered office be and is hereby fixed at [Address], Luxembourg, from the date of incorporation; that [Name] be and is hereby appointed as sole manager (gérant) with full authority to represent the company; and that the manager be authorized to complete all registration filings and open bank accounts. Further resolved that the initial corporate governance schedule be adopted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening a blocked capital account and obtaining the certificate of paid-up capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (banque agréée) selected by the founders; account-opening desk and relationship manager.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct each subscriber to transfer or deposit the agreed cash contribution into a dedicated blocked account opened in the name of the company in formation. Ensure that aggregate contributions equal or exceed EUR 12,000 and obtain from the bank a certificate of deposit or blocked-funds attestation evidencing that the capital is fully paid up and held subject to RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Bank KYC forms and source-of-funds evidence
Declaration of intended registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries or delays the account opening, cure by supplying corrected beneficial ownership declarations or enhanced source-of-funds evidence; alternatively select another Luxembourg bank and redeposit the capital.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and approval of the notarial deed and articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (notaire) engaged by the founders.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the draft articles of association to the notary for legal review and engrossment. Verify that the deed includes the corporate name, registered office, corporate purpose, share capital, shareholder details, manager appointment, duration, and decision-making provisions. Confirm compliance with mandatory SARL rules of the Law of 10 August 1915.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID copies of shareholders
Proof of right to use registered office (lease or owner consent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises a substantive objection, amend the draft articles, obtain missing consents, and resubmit the revised version for a new appointment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the incorporation deed before the Luxembourg notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary public in the district where execution takes place.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Attend the notarial appointment either in person or through a duly mandated attorney. Each subscriber must sign the deed; the notary verifies identity, legal capacity, and the paid-up capital certificate. After execution, the notary delivers an authentic copy and the engrossment required for RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney if any signatory is represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If execution is refused, cure by correcting the deed, producing a valid power of attorney, or resolving identity verification issues, then reschedule execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) online single filing platform; RCS registration department.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the single incorporation dossier electronically without delay after the notarial deed is signed. Transmit the authentic notarial copy, manager acceptance, beneficial owner declaration, registered office consent, and standardized RCS form. Complete the filing with a LuxTrust or eID electronic signature and pay the applicable RCS registration and publication fees.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS queries the application, file a corrective submission through the LBR portal with the requested supplemental documentation and an explanatory cover letter; the file is resumed once complete.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the official electronic compendium and receipt of RCS extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS Registry and the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA) publication office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, confirm that the incorporation deed excerpt has been published in RESA. Download the RCS certificate and extract of registration evidencing the legal existence, registration number, LEI-relevant data, and corporate details of the SARL.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed, contact the RCS through the LBR support channel with the file reference and registration proof to expedite the RESA publication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg one-stop shop (Guichet unique / MyGuichet.lu), Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), and Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for VAT (numéro de TVA) with the AEDT, enroll the company and any employees with the CCSS, and apply for a municipal establishment authorization (autorisation d'établissement) if physical premises or regulated activity are present. Confirm whether any creator-agency-specific permit is required; for pure administrative MCN activity, the RCS registration normally suffices.
required_dossiers: Registered office lease and municipal usages certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a permit is refused or queried, provide the requested documentation within the appeal window, and if necessary challenge the administrative decision before the competent administrative court within three months.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ISIC 7310 / NAICS 541810 creator agency and MCN activity; general economic oversight remains with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) and the commune for municipal establishment authorization.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sector-specific operating or manufacturing permit is required; a general municipal establishment authorization (autorisation d'établissement) may be necessary only for physical office premises falling within local business rules.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category 3 low-emission administrative office activity; no full EIA or environmental registration required in the absence of industrial processes, significant storage, or waste operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste emission sources expected; any sanitary wastewater must comply with municipal sewer connection rules and the general provisions of the Law of 19 December 2008 on water management; office HVAC systems, if installed, must satisfy the applicable energy performance and refrigerant standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (certificat de sécurité incendie) may be required by the commune for premises open to staff or the public; structural load inspection and building compliance are confirmed by the municipal construction department; occupational health clearance is coordinated by the Service national de la Santé au travail (State Occupational Health Service) when employees are engaged.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) for direct taxes and Administration de l’Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; centralized digital portal is MyGuichet.lu / guichet.lu and the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) for company registration
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entity establishes an SARL via the Luxembourg Business Registers to obtain the RCS matricule (business registration number); then file the incorporation dossier electronically with the AEDT for VAT registration and with the ACD for income tax identification, receiving a Luxembourg TIN / VAT identification number in the format LU00000000
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box exists in Luxembourg; a resident SARL is by default a fully taxable entity. Available elections include forming an intra-group VAT unity (assujetti unique) with related Luxembourg entities, and applying the EU Dioxide/hybrid mismatch rules which may require affirmative filing of information where an optional consolidation or equalization treatment is used; no standalone entity classification election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for Luxembourg-established small enterprises; non-resident suppliers have no threshold and must register for Luxembourg VAT where they make taxable supplies of digital services, distance sales or other activities deemed to be situated in Luxembourg
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not impose a real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping or continuous transaction controls (CTC) regime for private-sector B2B e-invoicing. B2B e-invoicing is permitted using authenticated formats (e.g. Peppol BIS) and is mandatory for suppliers to Luxembourg public-sector buyers under certain thresholds; all e-invoices must be stored in original format for audit purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to goods physically exported outside the European Union provided the exporter obtains proof of dispatch or transport within 90 days and supplies are made to an EU business customer or an equivalent consignee; services to non-EU business customers (including creator-agency, MCN and advertising services) are generally outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT under the place-of-supply rules, allowing input VAT recovery without applying Luxembourg VAT provided the customer’s non-EU business status is evidenced.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (via Luxembourg Customs / EU Single Administrative Document)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR or other transport evidence with signature and date
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/payment confirmation evidencing receipt of consideration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg tax and customs authorities may retroactively disallow zero-rating and assess Luxembourg VAT plus statutory interest; intentional fraudulent export claims subject to tax penalties (amende fiscale) and criminal sanctions, including potential imprisonment and fines, with joint liability of directors for concealment; mitigation requires full retention of contracts, invoices, customs declarations, transport evidence and incoming payment records.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (Central Bank of Luxembourg, BCL) in coordination with the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance and the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for foreign exchange and payments oversight
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies full capital and current account convertibility pursuant to EU Treaty provisions on free movement of capital and payments (Articles 63-65 TFEU). No exchange controls, no prior authorisation for foreign currency transactions, and no restrictions on profit remittance, dividend distribution, or liquidation proceeds for resident or non-resident shareholders. The euro is fully convertible; non-euro transactions are subject to standard market pricing and EU anti-money-laundering (AML) transparency obligations. Profit remittance hurdles are limited to corporate tax compliance, withholding tax obligations, and documentary proof of economic substance
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory timeline for export proceeds surrender, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no obligation to repatriate export receipts to a local bank account. Export revenues may be held in foreign currency accounts abroad, subject to general tax transparency and transfer pricing requirements. All settlements must comply with the EU Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) and international sanctions regimes

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-High subject to Luxembourg E-Money Institution (EMI) licensing under the CSSF or EU passporting from another Member State. Cross-border digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Payoneer) may provide ancillary settlement rails but are not recommended as sole treasury counterparties due to restricted KYC acceptance for creator payouts, lower transaction limits, and higher closure risk for high-volume MCN agency flows. A licensed EMI with SEPA and SWIFT capabilities, operating under a valid MiFID/EMD passport, can be used for small-value TikTok creator settlements, but principal operating liquidity should reside with a Tier-1 Luxembourg credit institution to ensure clearing reliability, negative interest rate exemptions, and correspondent banking access
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of at least one director (or a mandated representative with power of attorney) is generally required for the initial KYC interview at Luxembourg banks. However, most Tier-1 institutions allow remote onboarding via videoconference, digital identity verification, and apostilled corporate documents, provided the beneficial owner(s) and signatories pass enhanced due diligence (EDD). For an SARL with non-resident shareholders, a physical economic substance presence (registered office, local director or outsourcing arrangement) substantially reduces onboarding delays. Some banks require a local director or authorised signatory to appear in person before account activation, while others accept a certified copy of the passport plus a notarised board resolution. Remote opening is feasible in practice but subject to bank-specific risk appetite

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High cross-border creator payout aggregation (TikTok global payouts plus Wise B2B) may flag as unexpected 'peerto-peer' transaction patterns or potential money laundering through layering
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide audited contractual framework: (i) fully executed MCN talent agreements, (ii) TikTok creator payout statements with UETR (Unique End-to-End Transaction Reference) details, (iii) platform reconciliation reports from TikTok Creator Center, (iv) Wise B2B settlement records mapped to each creator, (v) a transfer pricing documentation file (OECD-compliant) demonstrating arm's-length commission deductions, (vi) corporate bank statements showing no mix of personal funds, and (vii) a written AML risk self-assessment confirming Low_Risk_Standard classification

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholders with crypto-adjacent or internet-gaming exposure, or source-of-wealth opacity in jurisdictions with AML deficiencies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver: (i) three years of bank statements of each non-resident shareholder, (ii) notarised source-of-wealth statement supported by audited financial statements, (iii) tax residence certificates (certificat de résidence fiscale), (iv) proof of business track record in advertising/ad-tech, (v) organisational chart with all ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) declared to the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), and (vi) a disciplined board resolution committing to no unlicensed money service activity

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: TikTok creator payouts arriving from multiple foreign jurisdictions (US, UK, SG, JP) with inconsistent remitter legal names trigger sanctions screening and false-positive name matches
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Establish an expected-transaction matrix listing all onboarding creator names, platform remitter aliases, and verified legal names; provide UK and EU sanctions screening evidence, DBA or trade-name registrations, and a designated compliance officer declaration; maintain a remediation procedure to resolve false positives within 48 hours with official sanctions-list FCA/OFAC/CSSF reference numbers

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injection to the Luxembourg SARL must be executed via SWIFT MT103 with clear economic purpose code. Recommended routing: non-resident shareholder's bank sends EUR via TARGET2 or SEPA Instant to the SARL's euro account at a Tier-1 Luxembourg bank. For foreign-currency injections, use SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'TREATY' (EU capital movement free-of-controls) and ensure the beneficiary reference includes 'Capital Subscription SARL' plus the corporate registration number (RCS Luxembourg). For capital increases, file a notarised deed with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register and register the UBO/subscription in the RBE. For shareholder loans, execute a written loan agreement with arm's-length interest rate and provide funds via MT103 with 'INTRACO' or 'CLOANB subsidy' purpose code to avoid reclassification as taxable equity
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for MCN agency services (creator commissions, royalty fees, and talent payments) must be settled through the following compliant rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for international bank transfers exceeding EUR 12,500 or outside SEPA; (ii) SEPA SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) for euro-denominated payouts to beneficiary accounts within EU/EEA; (iii) Commercial Letter of Credit (documentary collection L/C) where creator contracts exceed EUR 50,000 or require guarantee instruments; (iv) Wise B2B settlement API for low-value repetitive micro-payments to creators, subject to the EMI's periodic audit trail being exported and archived; (v) TikTok Creator Payout direct integration only for platform-owned distributor settlements, never as a principal treasury vehicle. All disbursements must include beneficiary name, IBAN or SWIFT BIC, and a structured remittance reference indicating the underlying creator contract ID to satisfy CSSF transaction monitoring and OECD CRS reporting
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (vanilla forwards) on EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/JPY with a Luxembourg credit institution or licensed investment firm, tenor aligned to expected TikTok payout dates
FX options (call/spread structures) for hedging potential adverse movements in creator revenue receipts from non-EU markets, subject to CSSF Sobriété rules on non-banking counterparties

Cross-currency swaps for swapping USD-denominated creator payout receivables into EUR, executed under ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a Tier-1 bank, to eliminate currency mismatch on the SARL's balance sheet

Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) are not permissible as a main instrument for EUR-based entities because EUR is fully convertible; however, NDFs may be used exceptionally for settlement of emerging-market creator revenues (e.g., TRY, ARS, NGN) where local currency convertibility is restricted, provided the bank has a valid derivative license and the transaction is booked as a hedge with documented underlying exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting (assemblée générale ordinaire) of shareholders – approval of the annual accounts, profit allocation, discharge of directors, and mandatory recording of minutes in the corporate minute book.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not a filing authority; signed minutes must be retained at the registered office and, where applicable, filed with the RCS in case of capital changes or director amendments.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be held within 6 months of the financial year end (i.e. by 30 June for calendar-year SARL); convening notice formalities vary for single-member SARL (sole shareholder adopts decisions by written instrument).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Nullity of resolutions adopted in violation of AGM rules, civil liability for directors who fail to call the meeting, and disqualification risk in proceedings for administrative strike-off of the company.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory auditor (réviseur d’entreprises agréé) is mandatory if, on the balance sheet date, the SARL exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds: (a) total balance sheet EUR 4,400,000 (approx. USD 4,840,000), (b) net turnover EUR 8,800,000 (approx. USD 9,680,000), (c) average workforce of 50 employees. A low-risk creator-incubation MCN with a simplified turnover of less than EUR 8.8 million is generally exempt.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2002 as amended, transposing EU Directive 2013/34/EU); IFRS optional for non-listed entities. The company must prepare single-entity accounts under the normal scheme or use the simplified legal scheme if under the abridged criteria.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must annually confirm and update the identity and shareholding percentages of all individuals holding more than 25% of the share capital or exercising control. This is performed by filing a new UBO declaration with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) within 6 months after the anniversary of the initial declaration. Any intermediary transfers must be reported within 30 days of the change. A physical register of UBOs must be maintained at the registered office.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (registre des administrateurs et gérants)
Minute Book (registre des procès-verbaux des assemblées et décisions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,600 – 3,800 (standard professional domiciliation and corporate agent fee for a Luxembourg SARL)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 (if below audit threshold) – USD 12,000 to 28,000 if the small-company audit threshold is exceeded

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate corporate income tax rate for Luxembourg City (composition: 17% CIT + 7% solidarity surcharge on CIT + 6.75% municipal business tax); municipal business tax rate varies by commune (6.75%–10.5%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP Box regime: 80% exemption of qualifying IP-derived net income, reducing the effective aggregate rate to approximately 4.98%. Participation exemption: 100% exemption of qualifying dividend income and capital gains from shareholdings of at least 10% (or acquisition cost of EUR 6 million) held for at least 12 months. Other incentives: capitalized R&D costs, innovation-related deductions, and enhanced tax depreciation for eligible digital and intellectual assets.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 500 (combined corporation income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax return) filed electronically via the eCDF (electronic Corporate Declarations) module on MyGuichet.lu; net wealth tax schedule annexed to Form 500.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is 31 December of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end (e.g., FY ending 31 December 2025: return due 31 December 2026); extensions may be granted on written request, and administrative penalties apply to late filers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the SARL, RCSL registration number, Luxembourg tax matricule, registered office address, activity code (ISIC/NACE 73.11 for advertising / creator agency), fiscal year start and end dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident entity with a Luxembourg permanent establishment (PE) must file using the PE registration number and certify the PE's local address and its representative (mandataire fiscal) with power of attorney.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net commercial result per the LUX GAAP (PCN) financial statements; reconciliation of statutory accounts to the tax result.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only profits attributable to the Luxembourg PE, computed on a separate-entity arm's-length basis, are reported; head-office allocations must be documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses to be added back: corporate income tax and municipal business tax paid, certain fines and penalties, non-deductible provisions, excessive or undocumented remuneration, TP adjustments, interest or royalties paid to an entity in an EU non-cooperative jurisdiction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add-backs apply equally to PE accounts; withholding tax on cross-border royalties or interest paid by the PE is nevertheless subject to the same domestic and treaty exemptions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of the participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains, the IP Box 80% exemption, utilization of loss carryforwards (17-year period), and tax-exempt subsidies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses may be deducted only if economically connected to the Luxembourg PE; treaty force-of-attraction limitations apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable income, application of 17% CIT, 7% solidarity surcharge, municipal business tax (commune-specific), and net wealth tax at 0.5% (minimum net wealth tax of EUR 3,570 applies even in loss years).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PEs are subject to the same rates on the Luxembourg-source taxable base; non-residents must attach the TRC of the foreign company and DTA allocation schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annexed certifications: beneficial ownership register (RBE) status, transfer pricing Master File and Local File availability declaration, and related-party transaction schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PEs must, on demand, produce the TP documentation of the foreign head office covering Luxembourg transactions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: automatic 10% surcharge (majoration d'office) on assessed tax plus late-payment interest of 0.6% per month (7.2% p.a.); administrative fines up to EUR 25,000 under Article 172 of the General Tax Law (AO); the tax authority may proceed to discretionary assessment (taxation d'office). Willful failure to file is exposed, under Article 179 AO, to criminal fines up to EUR 25,000 and imprisonment of eight days to five years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory dividend withholding tax, increased by the 7% solidarity surcharge to an effective 16.05% for non-exempt distributions; 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, the Luxembourg participation exemption, or applicable DTAs (e.g., 5% treaty rate for a 10% corporate shareholder, 15% otherwise).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief: (1) obtain a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the parent company's tax authority for the relevant fiscal year; (2) file Form 27 (demande d'exemption de retenue à la source) with the Luxembourg direct tax collector before dividend payment, attaching the TRC, proof of minimum 10% (or treaty-percentage) shareholding, proof of the 12-month holding period, and a certification of beneficial ownership; (3) the ACD issues an exemption certificate; (4) if WHT was already levied, a refund claim must be filed on the appropriate ACD form within the statutory period; anti-abuse (PPT / LOB) and economic substance documentation must be filed upon request.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% domestic Luxembourg withholding tax on royalty payments; 0% under the EU Interest-Royalties Directive (≥25% direct ownership) for related EU companies; DTA rates generally 0%–5%. Interest: 0% domestic WHT on paid debt interest; 15% WHT (plus solidarity surcharge) applies on interest and royalties paid to nondisclosing or non-cooperative jurisdictions and to certain hybrid structures under the Law of 21 December 2018.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full Master File and Local File must be prepared and filed where the Luxembourg entity belongs to a group with consolidated annual revenue of at least EUR 50,000,000; Country-by-Country Report (Form 800) is mandatory where consolidated group revenue equals or exceeds EUR 750,000,000. Documentation must be delivered to the ACD upon request (typically within 30 days); if not, penalties up to EUR 25,000 and TP re-adjustments apply.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg imposes no filing-based Economic Substance Regulations (BVI/Cayman model); however, substance is enforced through (i) the abuse-of-law doctrine (General Tax Law Article 6), (ii) EU ATAD / GAAR and the OECD MLI Principal Purpose Test, and (iii) transfer pricing substance requirements. An MCN / Agency SARL must demonstrate real activity in Luxembourg (own offices, qualified staff performing creator-representation and management functions, board and manager decisions taken in Luxembourg, adequate capital and operating expenditures) to access treaty benefits, the participation exemption, and the 0% EU dividend withholding regime. Substance deficiencies are recharacterized as artificial arrangements, triggering denial of treaty relief and immediate WHT re-assessments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission or false declaration of taxable revenue on Form 500, such as undisclosed TikTok creator payouts, fabricated deductible expenses, or fictitious losses to trigger or inflate loss carryforwards.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to EUR 25,000 and imprisonment of eight days to five years (Article 179 of the General Tax Law); mandatory re-assessment plus 10% late-filing or late-payment surcharge and 0.6% monthly interest; loss of the 17-year loss carryforward on abuse.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant / managing director who signs a false return is personally and jointly liable for the evaded tax, interest and penalties; Luxembourg courts may issue travel bans, seizure of personal assets, and director disqualification for the duration of the criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SARL as a letterbox entity: creator-management decisions and staff located outside Luxembourg while booking all profits in Luxembourg solely to use the participation exemption or treaty / Directive 0% WHT without genuine economic activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization as an abuse of law (Article 6 AO) with reassessment of the full corporate tax at the 24.94% aggregate rate; denial of treaty and EU-Directive relief; 15% WHT plus solidarity surcharge re-levied on distributions made during the relevant limitation window; fines up to EUR 25,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be declared jointly and severally liable for the company's unpaid tax and WHT under the de facto management doctrine; civil restitution of dividends paid out of artificially tax-exempt profits and personal fines for signing substance statements are imposed.
